processing: A flat-pressed special green made to Guizhou's provincial standard for flat green tea, DB52/T 442.3-2003, with a pan-roasted aroma.
harvest_season: Little is documented; flat greens of this kind are usually made from tender spring buds and leaves.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight, smooth and even, with a glossy jade-green colour.
appearance_wet: Bright tender green leaf, even and whole.
taste_profile: High, lasting aroma with a pan-roasted edge and a sweet taste.

brewing.notes: General guidance for flat greens, as with Long Jing: add the leaf to warm water in a glass or gaiwan and avoid boiling water.

vintage_note: Usual for flat Chinese greens: sold as the current spring harvest and best drunk within about a year. It comes in small quantities and may appear under the Qingshuitang trademark rather than as a general regional product.
description:
Qingchi Cuipian is a flat green tea from Guizhou, usually linked to Qingchi town in Jinsha County. One account files it under nearby Qixingguan District instead, so the exact home needs care.

It follows the provincial standard for flat green tea, giving straight, smooth, glossy leaf. Think of the family resemblance to Long Jing in shape, though it is its own tea, with no published detail on the specific steps.

The description is high in aroma with a pan-roasted edge and a sweet taste, in a bright yellow-green liquor. Treat it gently: water around 80 to 85°C, and an open vessel so the leaf is not stewed.

It is rarely seen outside Guizhou. Output was reported as small, with one producer's annual capacity at 10 tonnes, so ask who made it and when it was picked. It is sometimes named among Guizhou's ten famous teas, though such lists vary by publisher.
history: Little is documented about when this particular tea was created. Reports credit it with a gold award at a 2010 Shanghai tea culture festival, and the Qingshuitang trademark is tied to it.
